findings: Core entities—Opportunity, Assessment, Proposal, Authorization, Execution, Audit, Outcome, Evolution Patch, Quest Candidate, Quest, Authorization Receipt, and Audit Event—are identifiable and increasingly contract-bound.
Quest semantics are materially stronger than the older phase vocabulary because lifecycle states and work-acceptance meaning are explicit.
The repository lacks a single canonical ontology registry linking legacy phase artifacts to the newer domain/application/infrastructure model.
Phase numbering is non-contiguous and documentation names Phase 1 and Phase 9 while the executable phase registry omits them.
Risk, authority, lifecycle, evidence-strength, runtime-mode, and connector classes exist but are distributed across schemas, configs, docs, and code.
Legacy phase taxonomy and Quest/domain taxonomy overlap without an explicit equivalence or supersession map.
Contract-first, fail-closed, human-in-the-loop, audit-first, idempotency, optimistic revision control, and local-only execution are consistently present.
Multiple quality/evolution phases appear to implement adjacent review concepts, increasing pathway length and duplicate interpretation risk.
The production-readiness ledger correctly distinguishes structural evidence from operational proof.
The newer Quest vertical slice follows domain/application/infrastructure/API separation and explicit composition.
The repository currently operates two persistence substrates: memory/aigc_state.sqlite for the legacy runtime and .aigc/local_operator.sqlite3 for the Quest/API slice.
The large Quest application service centralizes lifecycle, authorization-bundle construction, terminal decisions, and validation; this is reviewable now but will become a change-coupling hotspot.
External action remains blocked and operator review is explicit.
Quest work acceptance is separated from external contract acceptance and delivery acceptance.
Production identity, live connector, deployment, and tenant isolation authority remain absent and must not be inferred from local fixtures.
